title: TranscriptFormer: Generative Cell Atlas Foundation Model Trained Across 112M Cells and 1.5 Billion Years of Evolution
whyItMatters: Published in Science, TranscriptFormer trained on 112 million cells across 12 species spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution—transferring cell-type annotations across >685M years of divergence and spotting human disease states zero-shot.
summary: Published in Science on July 2, 2026 (Vol. 393, Issue 6806, ead/aec8514, doi:10.1126/science.aec8514, PMID 42096520), James D. Pearce, Sara E. Simmonds, Stephen Quake, and colleagues at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and Stanford University introduced TranscriptFormer, a family of generative single-cell foundation models trained on 112 million cells from 12 diverse species spanning 1.53 billion years of evolutionary history. By pairing protein-embedding gene representations with a generative transformer over joint gene-identity and expression distributions, TranscriptFormer learns conserved transcriptional programs across distantly related kingdoms and phyla. It transfers cell-type annotations accurately across more than 685 million years of evolutionary distance, predicts cell-type-specific transcription factor and gene-regulatory interactions without supervision, and identifies infected or diseased human cell states zero-shot.
technicalHighlights: Pretrained on 112 million single cells spanning 12 species and 1.53 billion years of evolutionary divergence in a unified generative transformer.
Transfers cell-type annotations accurately across >685 million years of evolutionary separation without species-specific supervision.
Identifies human disease and pathogen-infected cell states zero-shot and infers cell-type-specific transcription factor programs.
caveats: Evaluates observational transcriptomic atlases rather than direct causal intervention outcomes; clinical disease-state diagnostics require prospective validation.

scoreRationale.foundational: Establishes a generative evolutionary foundation model spanning 1.53 billion years of cellular transcriptomes in a single probabilistic framework.
scoreRationale.ripple: Accelerates cross-species cell-atlas annotation, evolutionary developmental biology, and zero-shot disease-state detection across human tissues.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science with systematic cross-species transfer, gene-regulation, and human disease benchmarks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Enables instant zero-shot annotation and generative transcriptomic querying across 112M-cell evolutionary scale.
